q: What time do I show up on my first day and what should I bring?
answer: On your first day, report to the HR office (lower lobby, next to the employee entrance) at 8:30 am. Bring two forms of ID for your I-9 paperwork, your bank details for direct deposit, and closed-toe, non-slip shoes. HR will issue your employee ID badge, locker assignment and uniform. Your manager will meet you at 10:30 am for a property tour.

q: how many shifts do i shadow before working alone
answer: You'll shadow a trainer for at least three shifts before working alone. This is part of your first-week tasks, and your manager will check in with you at the end of week one.

q: What do I need to pass in my first month?
answer: In your first 30 days, you need to pass the menu and allergen knowledge check (80% to pass; you may retake it once). You also need to complete the guest service training "LEARN" (section 5.1); and have a 30-day review with your manager. If you're in an alcohol-serving position, you must also complete responsible alcohol service certification within 30 days of hire; the resort pays the course fee.

q: When do schedules come out?
answer: Schedules are posted every Wednesday by 5 pm for the following Monday-Sunday week, in the scheduling app and on the board outside the kitchen office. Check your schedule before every shift; changes after posting are sent through the app.

q: Can I just trade shifts with someone?
answer:
Yes, but only with a coworker in the same position, and only once your manager approves it:

1. Post the swap in the scheduling app; it only counts once your manager approves it.
2. Until it is approved, you are still responsible for the original shift.
3. Swaps that would put either person over 40 hours in a week need manager approval because of overtime.

q: I'm sick, my shift starts at 5pm. When do I need to call?
answer: You need to call by 1 pm. If you cannot work a shift, call the outlet manager's line at least 4 hours before your start time. Note that texting a coworker is not a call-out.

q: Is texting my coworker enough to call out?
answer: No, texting a coworker is not a call-out. If you cannot work a shift, call the outlet manager's line at least 4 hours before your start time (2 hours for morning shifts starting before 8 am). Two no-call/no-shows within 90 days may lead to termination.

q: My buddy said he can clock me in if I'm running late. Is that ok?
answer: No, that's not allowed. Never clock in or out for another employee. Instead, if you are running late, call before your start time, using the outlet manager's line. Texting a coworker is not a call-out.

q: I forgot to clock out last night. What should I do?
answer:
Tell your manager right away so they can fix the punch. The handbook says if you forget to clock in or out, tell your manager the same day so they can fix the punch; do not wait until payday.

If your paycheck still looks wrong afterward, contact HR within 7 days of payday at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: I'm 17. When do I get my lunch break?
answer: Because you're under 18, you must take a 30-minute meal break after 5 hours of work. Clock out for meal breaks; do not clock out for rest breaks. You also receive one paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked.

q: Do I get paid for my 10 minute break?
answer: Yes. Employees also receive one paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked. Clock out for meal breaks; do not clock out for rest breaks.

q: When does overtime kick in?
answer: Overtime is paid for hours over 40 in a Monday-Sunday workweek, at 1.5 times your regular rate. All overtime must be approved by your manager in advance. Working unapproved overtime is still paid, but may lead to corrective action. Also note that swaps that would put either person over 40 hours in a week need manager approval because of overtime.

q: When is payday?
answer: Pay is every other Friday by direct deposit. Pay stubs are available in the HR portal. If your paycheck looks wrong, contact HR within 7 days of payday. HR is at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: I'm a busser. How do I get tips?
answer: As a busser, you don't keep tips directly. Bussers, food runners and hosts receive a share of the tip pool: servers contribute 3% of their food and beverage sales, and bartenders contribute 2% of their sales. The pool is paid out with your paycheck. Pay is every other Friday by direct deposit. Pay stubs are available in the HR portal. If your paycheck looks wrong, contact HR within 7 days of payday. You can reach Human Resources (HR) at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: Do managers get a cut of the tip pool?
answer: No. Managers never take part in the tip pool. Bussers, food runners and hosts receive a share of the tip pool: servers contribute 3% of their food and beverage sales, and bartenders contribute 2% of their sales.

q: I work about 25 hours a week. Can I get medical insurance?
answer: No, at about 25 hours a week you wouldn't qualify for medical coverage. Medical, dental and vision coverage is for full-time employees (averaging 30 or more hours a week), and part-time employees are not eligible for medical coverage but may join the retirement savings plan after 90 days. For benefits questions, contact Human Resources (HR) at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: I want Dec 26 off to see family. Can I request it?
answer:
Yes, you can request it, but Dec 26 falls in a blackout period, so it may be denied.

- **How to request:** Request time off in the scheduling app at least 3 weeks before the date.
- **Blackout:** Requests are approved first-come, first-served, and may be denied during blackout periods: the week of Christmas through New Year's Day, Easter weekend, and the Fourth of July. Requesting early may help.
- **Timing:** You will get an answer in the app within 7 days of your request. Do not book travel until your request is approved.

q: How far ahead do I need to request vacation?
answer: Request time off in the scheduling app at least 3 weeks before the date. Requests are approved first-come, first-served, and may be denied during blackout periods: the week of Christmas through New Year's Day, Easter weekend, and the Fourth of July. You will get an answer in the app within 7 days of your request. Do not book travel until your request is approved.

q: Do I get extra pay if I work Thanksgiving?
answer: Yes. Employees who work on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving or Christmas Day are paid 1.5 times their regular rate for hours worked that day.

q: A guest is mad their food was cold. Can I comp their whole meal?
answer:
No, you can't comp the whole meal yourself. You may offer a complimentary dessert or non-alcoholic drink up to $15 to resolve a complaint. Anything more, including comping a meal or a room charge, needs a manager. Even the $15 comp needs a manager's approval code in the POS.

Handle the complaint with LEARN: Listen without interrupting; Empathize ("I'm sorry this happened"); Apologize; Resolve, or find someone who can; Notify your manager so they can follow up.

q: guest might be having an allergic reaction what do i do
answer: If a guest has an allergic reaction, call security at extension 5555 immediately. They are trained in first aid and will call 911 if needed. Do not move an injured person unless they are in danger.

q: Someone looks about 35. Do I need to card them?
answer: Yes. Check ID for anyone who looks under 40. Accept only valid, unexpired government photo IDs. The legal drinking age in Hawaii is 21.

q: Can I wear sneakers?
answer:
The handbook doesn't mention sneakers specifically, but it does set the shoe requirement: Black, closed-toe, non-slip shoes are required in all F&B areas. Any shoes you wear on shift need to meet all three of those criteria.

q: I hurt my hand at work but it's minor. Do I need to report it?
answer: Yes. If you are injured at work, tell your manager right away, even if it seems minor, and complete an incident report before the end of your shift.

q: How do I report harassment anonymously?
answer: You can report harassment anonymously by calling the Ethics Line at 1-800-555-0199. You can also report it to your manager or to HR (extension 4100). You will not be punished for reporting in good faith.

q: Where do employees park and how much is it?
answer: Employees park in the employee lot on Example Beach Road, not in the guest garage. A monthly employee parking pass costs $25 through payroll deduction; sign up with HR. If you take the bus instead, the resort reimburses half of a monthly bus pass; bring your receipt to HR.

q: Can I eat the leftover buffet food after brunch?
answer: No. Employees may not eat food from the kitchen, buffet or guest areas, including leftovers. Instead, one free meal is provided per shift in the employee cafeteria.

q: What temp does the walk-in need to be?
answer: The walk-in cooler must be at 41°F or below. Check and log walk-in cooler and freezer temperatures at opening and closing on the clipboard by the door. If the walk-in reads above 41°F, tell the chef or MOD immediately and do not serve food from it until it is checked.

q: Can I void an item after I sent it to the kitchen?
answer: No, servers cannot void an item after it is sent to the kitchen. Ask a manager to void it and give the reason (kitchen error, guest changed mind, etc.). All voids and comps appear on the nightly manager report.

q: My drawer is $3 short. Do I have to report it?
answer: No, the SOPs don't require you to report a $3 shortage. They say to report any shortage over $5 to the manager before clocking out. You still need to count your bank at the start and end of the shift with a manager present, so your manager will be there for the end-of-shift count anyway.
